original.target_description: Experiment 4: composite current positive emotion during anticipation versus retrospection of hypothetical ski vacation

n.exclusions: No exclusions reported for this test; anticipation n = 45 and retrospection n = 50.

replication.target_description: Hypothetical resort vacation: composite influence on current mood (Mean of DV1), anticipation versus retrospection

n.location: p. 39, Table 8a, Vacation (all three component measures have identical group Ns)
n.sample_role: participants by anticipation and retrospection condition, respectively; printed group counts
n.exclusions: General funneling removed two participants unable to mentally time travel and two unable to write about a scenario (p. 38). Main results explicitly described as pre-exclusion on p. 37; subsequent supplementary exclusions are not applied to these printed tests.

es.location: p. 40, Table 9a, Vacation / Mean of DV1

p.location: p. 40, Table 9a, Vacation / Mean of DV1

reported_success.quote: we found support in menstruation (d = 0.46, 95% CI [0.20, 0.73] and vacation (d = 0.18, 95% CI [0.01, 0.35]).

notes: Extracted by neutral outcome description; supplied replication page locators interchange current emotion (DV1, p. 40) and predicted/remembered emotion (DV2, p. 41). No values converted. Replication main tables report pre-exclusion analyses, apart from general funneling. Supplied neutral descriptions for 1746 and 1747 both identify the current-emotion contrast in Experiment 4; no distinct tests can be established from their wording, so both retain the same matching composite test. Original additionally reports predicted/remembered enjoyment d = 0.14, p = .507 and a covariate-adjusted temporal-perspective contrast d = 0.45, p = .032; neither substituted for the neutral description. Replication changed ski vacation to generic resort vacation (p. 35). Authors narrative support for vacation refers to the mood component (d = 0.18), whereas composite DV1 p = .074; Authors narrative verdict is successful for vacation overall; it is not a specific verdict on the composite DV1 test, and its quoted support refers to a different component.
